verses.text: Gaia, Earth, hid her son Cronus in ambush and placed in his hands
a jagged-toothed sickle, then told him the whole plan.
Then mighty Uranus, Sky, came bringing night, and over Earth,
longing for lovemaking, he settled and stretched himself
in every direction. From his hiding place, his son reached out
with his left hand; with his right he seized the enormous sickle,
long and jagged-toothed, and his own father's genitals
he swiftly sliced away, flinging them back
behind him. They did not leave his hand in vain:
every drop of blood that scattered
Earth caught, and as the years rolled round,
she bore the mighty Erinyes, spirits of vengeance, and the great Giants,
gleaming in armor, holding long spears in their hands,
and the nymphs called Meliae, ash-tree spirits, across the boundless earth.
Once Cronus had cut off the genitals with adamant, an unbreakable material,
and thrown them from the land into the surging sea,
they drifted over the water for a long time. White
foam rose around the immortal flesh, and within it a girl
grew. First she drew near holy Cythera,
then from there she reached Cyprus, surrounded by the sea.
Out stepped a beautiful goddess, worthy of reverence, and grass
grew beneath her slender feet. They call her Aphrodite,
the foam-born goddess and Cytherea of the lovely crown,
gods and humans alike, because she grew in foam, called aphros in Greek;
and Cytherea because she came to Cythera;
and Cyprus-born because she was born on wave-washed Cyprus;
and Genital-loving because she appeared from genitals.
Eros, Love, went with her, and beautiful Himeros, Desire, followed
from her birth, as she went to join the company of gods.
From the beginning, Aphrodite has held this honor and been allotted
this share among humans and immortal gods:
young women's intimate whispers, smiles and deceptions,
sweet pleasure, lovemaking, and tenderness.
Their father gave these children the name Titans,
mighty Uranus, Sky, rebuking those he himself had fathered.
He said they had strained in their recklessness to do a monstrous
deed, and punishment for it would come in time.
Night bore hateful Moros, Doom, and black Ker, a spirit of death,
and Thanatos, Death; she bore Hypnos, Sleep, and the tribe of Dreams.
The dark goddess Night bore them without sleeping with anyone.
Then she bore Momus, Blame, and Oizys, painful Misery,
and the Hesperides, who tend, beyond the famed river Oceanus,
the beautiful golden apples and the trees that bear that fruit.
She also bore the Fates and the Keres, merciless avengers,
Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos, who give mortals
their share of good and bad when they are born,
and pursue the wrongdoing of humans and gods.
These goddesses never let their terrible anger rest
until they make whoever has done wrong pay dearly.
Deadly Night also bore Nemesis, Payback, a scourge to mortal humans;
after Nemesis she bore Apate, Deceit, and Philotes, Intimacy,
and destructive Old Age, and Eris, fierce-hearted Strife.
